statements: Muslims fast during the month of Ramadan.
The fast begins at dawn and ends at sunset.
The fast begins at sunset and ends at dawn.
easy.explain: The fast runs from the break of dawn until sunset. Eating is permitted during the night.

statements: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in Makkah.
The Qur'an was revealed in Arabic.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ could not be described as a messenger.
easy.explain: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a messenger of Allah; affirming this is part of the shahada itself.

statements: There are 114 surahs in the Qur'an.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the first surah in the mushaf.
easy.explain: Al-Fatihah is the first surah. Al-Baqarah is the second, and the longest at 286 ayahs.

statements: Eid al-Fitr comes at the end of Ramadan.
Eid al-Adha comes during the month of Hajj.
Eid al-Adha comes at the end of Ramadan.
easy.explain: Eid al-Fitr ends Ramadan, on 1 Shawwal. Eid al-Adha falls on 10 Dhul-Hijjah, during the days of Hajj.

statements: Muslims pray facing the Ka'bah.
The Ka'bah is in Makkah.
Muslims pray facing Madinah.
easy.explain: The qiblah is the Ka'bah in Makkah, not Madinah. Madinah holds the Prophet's mosque but is not the direction of prayer.

statements: Zakat is given to those in need.
Zakat is one of the five pillars.
Zakat is a voluntary charity with no fixed rules.
easy.explain: Zakat is obligatory, with a defined threshold (nisab), rate and set of eligible recipients. The voluntary charity is sadaqah.

statements: Jumu'ah prayer is held on Friday.
Jumu'ah is preceded by a sermon.
Jumu'ah prayer is held on Saturday.
easy.explain: Jumu'ah is the Friday congregational prayer, and it is preceded by the khutbah.

statements: Wudu is performed before prayer.
Wudu involves washing the face, arms and feet.
Wudu is performed only once a year.
easy.explain: Wudu is performed whenever it has been invalidated and prayer is to be offered — potentially several times a day.

statements: The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
The Tawrat was given to Prophet Musa.
The Zabur was given to Prophet Isa.
easy.explain: The Zabur was given to Prophet Dawud. Prophet Isa was given the Injil.

statements: Hajj is performed in Dhul-Hijjah.
Umrah can be performed at any time of year.
Hajj can be performed at any time of year.
easy.explain: Hajj has a fixed season in Dhul-Hijjah. It is Umrah that may be performed at any time.

statements: Fajr is prayed before sunrise.
Maghrib is prayed after sunset.
Isha is prayed before Maghrib.
easy.explain: Isha comes after Maghrib. The order through the day is Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha.

statements: The Ka'bah is a cube-shaped structure.
Pilgrims walk around the Ka'bah seven times.
Pilgrims walk around the Ka'bah three times.
easy.explain: Tawaf consists of seven circuits around the Ka'bah.

statements: Angels are created beings.
Jibril brought revelation to the prophets.
Jibril was a prophet sent to his own people.
easy.explain: Jibril is an angel, not a prophet. Prophets are human beings chosen from among their own people.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah is recited in every rak'ah.
Surah Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs.
Surah Al-Fatihah is the last surah in the Qur'an.
easy.explain: Al-Fatihah is the first surah. The last is An-Nas, surah 114.

statements: The shahada has two parts.
Saying the shahada sincerely is how one enters Islam.
The shahada is one of the pillars of iman.
easy.explain: The shahada is the first of the five pillars of Islam. The articles of iman are a separate list of six beliefs.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf is often recited on Fridays.
Surah Al-Kahf has 110 ayahs.
Surah Al-Kahf is a Madinan surah.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Kahf is Makkan. It has 110 ayahs and is commonly recited on Fridays.

statements: Juz 30 begins with Surah An-Naba.
The Qur'an is divided into 30 ajza.
The Qur'an is divided into 40 ajza.
medium.explain: The Qur'an is conventionally divided into 30 ajza, the thirtieth beginning at Surah An-Naba.

statements: Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs.
Al-Kawthar has three ayahs.
Al-Ikhlas has six ayahs.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Ikhlas has four ayahs. Al-Kawthar, with three, is the shortest surah.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ was about forty at the first revelation.
Revelation continued for about twenty-three years.
Revelation continued for about ten years.
medium.explain: Revelation continued for approximately twenty-three years: roughly thirteen in Makkah and ten in Madinah.

statements: The Makkan period lasted about thirteen years.
The Madinan period lasted about ten years.
The Madinan period lasted about twenty years.
medium.explain: The Madinan period ran from the Hijrah in 622 CE to the Prophet's passing in 632 CE — about ten years.

statements: Eid al-Adha falls on 10 Dhul-Hijjah.
The Day of Arafah falls on 9 Dhul-Hijjah.
The Day of Arafah falls on 10 Dhul-Hijjah.
medium.explain: Arafah is 9 Dhul-Hijjah; Eid al-Adha is the following day, the 10th.

statements: Surah Yasin is surah 36.
Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55.
Surah Al-Mulk is surah 77.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Mulk is surah 67. Surah 77 is Al-Mursalat.

statements: Sa'i is performed between Safa and Marwah.
Sa'i consists of seven circuits.
Sa'i is performed around the Ka'bah.
medium.explain: Walking around the Ka'bah is Tawaf. Sa'i is the seven circuits between the hills of Safa and Marwah.

statements: Masjid al-Aqsa was the first qiblah.
The qiblah was changed to the Ka'bah in the Madinan period.
The qiblah was changed to the Ka'bah before the Hijrah.
medium.explain: The change of qiblah took place after the Hijrah, during the Madinan period, and is referred to in Surah Al-Baqarah.

statements: Abu Bakr was given the title as-Siddiq.
Umar ibn al-Khattab was given the title al-Faruq.
Uthman ibn Affan was given the title al-Faruq.
medium.explain: Al-Faruq was the title of Umar. Uthman is known as Dhun-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights.

statements: Surah At-Tawbah does not open with the Basmalah.
Surah At-Tawbah is a Madinan surah.
Surah At-Tawbah is the shortest surah in the Qur'an.
medium.explain: At-Tawbah has 129 ayahs and is one of the longer surahs. The shortest is Al-Kawthar.

statements: There are six articles of faith.
There are five pillars of Islam.
There are six pillars of Islam.
medium.explain: There are five pillars of Islam and six articles of iman. The six is the articles of faith, not the pillars.

statements: Laylat al-Qadr is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan.
Surah Al-Qadr describes it as better than a thousand months.
Laylat al-Qadr falls on a fixed, known date every year.
medium.explain: Its exact night is not fixed in the sources. It is sought across the last ten nights, most commonly on the odd-numbered ones.

statements: Zakat is commonly 2.5% on qualifying savings.
Zakat becomes due after a lunar year has passed.
Zakat is due on all wealth, with no minimum threshold.
medium.explain: Zakat is due only on wealth above the nisab threshold. Below it, no zakat is owed.

statements: The Hijri calendar is lunar.
The Hijri year is shorter than the Gregorian year.
The Hijri year is longer than the Gregorian year.
medium.explain: A lunar year is roughly 354 days, about eleven days shorter than the Gregorian year — which is why Ramadan moves earlier each year.

statements: Surah Al-Baqarah has 286 ayahs.
Surah Al-Imran has 200 ayahs.
Surah An-Nisa has 200 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah An-Nisa has 176 ayahs. Al-Imran is the one with 200.

statements: Surah Al-An'am has 165 ayahs.
Surah Al-A'raf has 206 ayahs.
Surah Al-Ma'idah has 165 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ma'idah has 120 ayahs. It is Al-An'am that has 165.

statements: Surah Maryam is surah 19.
Surah Ta-Ha is surah 20.
Surah Al-Anbiya is surah 20.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Anbiya is surah 21. Surah 20 is Ta-Ha.

statements: Badr was fought in Ramadan of 2 AH.
Uhud was fought in 3 AH.
The conquest of Makkah took place in 6 AH.
hard.explain: The conquest of Makkah took place in Ramadan of 8 AH. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was the event of 6 AH.

statements: Mu'tah was fought in 8 AH.
Tabuk took place in 9 AH.
Khaybar took place in 9 AH.
hard.explain: Khaybar took place in 7 AH, shortly after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

statements: Abu Bakr's caliphate began in 11 AH.
Umar's caliphate began in 13 AH.
Uthman's caliphate began in 13 AH.
hard.explain: Uthman's caliphate began in 23 AH, after Umar's roughly ten-year rule.

statements: Surah Al-Kawthar has three ayahs.
Surah Al-Asr has three ayahs.
Surah An-Nasr has four ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah An-Nasr has three ayahs, like Al-Kawthar and Al-Asr.

statements: Juz 30 runs from An-Naba to An-Nas.
Juz 30 contains 37 surahs.
Juz 29 begins with Surah Al-Mulk, surah 68.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Mulk is surah 67, and juz 29 does begin with it. The surah number given is wrong; 68 is Al-Qalam.

statements: Surah Al-Fil refers to the Year of the Elephant.
Surah Quraysh follows Surah Al-Fil in the mushaf.
Surah Quraysh precedes Surah Al-Fil in the mushaf.
hard.explain: Al-Fil is surah 105 and Quraysh is surah 106, so Quraysh follows it.

statements: Surah Yusuf tells one continuous narrative.
Surah Yusuf has 111 ayahs.
Surah Yusuf is a Madinan surah.
hard.explain: Surah Yusuf is Makkan. It has 111 ayahs and is distinctive for telling a single sustained narrative.

statements: Al-Bukhari died in 870 CE.
Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj died in 875 CE.
Abu Dawud compiled one of the two Sahih collections.
hard.explain: The two Sahih collections are those of al-Bukhari and Muslim. Abu Dawud compiled a Sunan, one of the other four of the six books.

statements: Abu Hanifah died in 767 CE.
Malik ibn Anas died in 795 CE.
Al-Shafi'i died before Abu Hanifah.
hard.explain: Al-Shafi'i died in 820 CE, over fifty years after Abu Hanifah. The usual order is Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafi'i, then Ahmad ibn Hanbal.

statements: Surah Ar-Rahman's refrain appears 31 times.
Surah Al-Mursalat also has a repeated refrain.
Surah Ar-Rahman is a surah of juz 30.
hard.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55 and falls in juz 27. Al-Mursalat does have its own repeated refrain.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ passed away in Rabi al-Awwal.
The Hijrah took place in the month of Rabi al-Awwal.
The Hijri calendar begins its year with Rabi al-Awwal.
hard.explain: The Hijri year begins with Muharram. The calendar counts from the year of the Hijrah, but its first month is Muharram, not the month of the migration itself.

statements: Surah Al-Isra is also known as Bani Isra'il.
Surah Al-Isra has 111 ayahs.
Surah Al-Isra is also known as Surah Al-Mi'raj.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Isra (17) is also called Bani Isra'il. 'Surah Al-Mi'raj' is not one of its recognised names.
